principles: Keep resolveWaveSafety a pure projector — no store I/O inside it; compute overlap data at the call site.
Extract pure exported helpers for both surfaces so the smoke is hermetic (no store, no git).
Advisory-only: never raise blockerCount, never read the gate block field at REVIEW.
Reuse existing primitives (computeWriteSet, globsOverlap, evaluateDecompositionGate, TERMINAL_PHASES, schedulingDegradation) — add no new overlap logic.
Mirror the active-peer semantics of evaluateDecompositionGate (self asserts parallelSafe=yes; peer non-terminal and asserts parallelSafe=yes).
drivers: resolveWaveSafety is private + pure (must stay testable without store)
Advisory must not touch blockerCount / signed review.json
Must consume already-frozen Stories 0-3 functions unchanged

options.name: pure-helpers
pros: hermetic smoke without a fake StoryStore

options.name: inline-with-store
cons: resolveWaveSafety would need store I/O OR the smoke needs a full fake StoryStore + git probe — not hermetic
harder to unit-test the overlap/advisory logic in isolation

rationale: Extracting computeScopeGlobOverlaps(self, peers) and decompositionAdvisoryIssues(story, peers, contracts, cfg) as pure exported helpers keeps resolveWaveSafety a pure projector, makes both advisory surfaces unit-testable hermetically (no StoryStore/git), and matches the pure-function + thin-call-site-wiring pattern used by Stories 1-3. The call sites (storyRef, story_review handler) do the store reads and pass plain data in.

preMortem.scenario: The scope_glob_overlap degradation accidentally fires for a story with no asserted parallelism or against a DONE/DISCARDED peer, spamming the wave projection
preMortem.trigger: computeScopeGlobOverlaps forgets the self.parallelSafe===yes guard or the TERMINAL_PHASES peer filter
preMortem.consequence: noisy false-positive warnings erode operator trust in the advisory
preMortem.mitigation: guard on self.parallelSafe===yes AND filter peers by !TERMINAL_PHASES.has(phase) && peer.parallelSafe===yes; smoke asserts zero overlaps for non-parallel self and terminal/non-parallel peers

preMortem.scenario: The advisory injection accidentally raises blockerCount and changes the signed review.json
preMortem.trigger: pushing the gate advisories at severity blocker, or also pushing the gate block field
preMortem.consequence: a non-blocking advisory becomes a hard REVIEW blocker, breaking the spec contract
preMortem.mitigation: push only advisories[] at severity advisory; never read the block field; smoke asserts the produced issues are all severity advisory and that blockerCount (filter severity===blocker) is unchanged

preMortem.scenario: A missing/unreadable peer scope contract throws and crashes the wave projection or story_review
preMortem.trigger: store.readScopeContract returns null and the call-site code dereferences it, or computeWriteSet receives null
preMortem.consequence: wave projection / REVIEW crashes on real projects with legacy stories lacking contracts
preMortem.mitigation: null-tolerant: skip peers whose contract is null when building write-sets (a missing peer contract is handled by evaluateDecompositionGate per §4.8); smoke includes a peer with no contract and asserts no throw
